newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks continue drop on Mideast uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks continue drop on Mideast uncertainty.

text.p: Jordanian stocks continued their drop on Tuesday as regional political tension sparked by Israeli-Palestinian unrest kept investors away, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index dropped 0.24 percent to 147.60 points from 147.95 points on Monday.
A total of 214,766 shares changed hands for 456,910 dinars ($651,000) in select buying of blue chips.

"The market's performance continues to be very week because of the region's political events," said one dealer. "This has helped keep foreign investors and institutional buyers away from the market leaving business to floor traders who have been very tight on cash for months".

King Hussein, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat are set to attend a summit in Washington later on Tuesday called by U.S. President Bill Clinton to try and salvage Middle East peace.
Israel opened a second entrance to a tourist tunnel in Jerusalem near Moslem holy sites last Tuesday, sparking gun battles and clashes that claimed 57 Palestinian and 15 Israeli lives.

After gradual gains earlier this month that sent the market back above 150 points last week for the first time in four months, shares began to hit down-limits last week with stock moving lower in thin volume.
Brokers fear the market may be running out of steam as institutional investors continue to wait in the sidelines and stocks run into profit-taking after the bourse's recent results-driven rally.

The market, one of the most politically sensitive bourses in the region, was hit this year by the breakdown of Middle East peace talks and the delay in implementing a limited oil-for-food deal with Jordan's biggest trading partner Iraq.
It is working on a wider package of reforms aimed at making the stock exchange, on a downward trend for two years after a 1992-93 bull run, more efficient, and investor-friendly.

A draft law is due to be put before Jordan's parliament soon which would tighten up regulations on accountability and transparency both for brokers and listed companies on the Amman Financial Market (AFM).
Industrials dominated trade on Tuesday, followed by banks and services.
Market leader Arab Bank which propelled the index upwards in the first half of September, remained unchanged at 242 dinars. The Middle East Investment Bank fell .03 to 1.06 dinars.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.43 percent to 81.26 points, still 14.92 percent down from the same time last year.
